who_can_apply: Ages 13 and 14 may volunteer only with an adult who is also a volunteer. Ages 15 and 16 may volunteer on their own, but an adult must attend orientation with them. The page gives no general rule for 17 year olds.
how_to_apply: Fill out the individual volunteer application, then go to orientation. A criminal background check is part of orientation. Email animalservicesvolunteers@austintexas.gov for help.
notes: Read the volunteer handbook linked on the page first.
duration: At least 6 hours per month
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers give at least 6 hours a month.

who_can_apply: Austin, TX residents who attend an Austin-area high school, ages 15 to 18 when applying, available for the whole program with no more than 3 days absent.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application (link posted on the page) with an essay. Choose your preferred track on the application. Email SummerHSIntern@austintexas.gov with questions.
notes: Separate from the Austin ISD / Austin Chamber paid internship. Placements depend on site access and career interest.
duration: 6 weeks (June 1 to July 10 in 2026)
pay_detail: $13 per hour, 20 hours per week

who_can_apply: Teen artists. The page does not give ages, grades or other rules.
how_to_apply: Email lindsay@creativeaction.org to ask how to join.
notes: Ask about ages, schedule, pay and cost before you plan on it. Creative Action also lists the Changing Lives Youth Theatre Ensemble for teens.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Pay or cost is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 19 who live in Austin. Must be able to commit to the full internship. Acceptance depends on the City of Austin document check and New Employee Orientation.
how_to_apply: No application is open now. Join the mailing list on the page, or read the FAQ PDF. Questions go to the email link on the page.
notes: The age range on the page is 17 to 19. The page calls applicants high school students. It does not state pay, grades or a 2027 application window. Check when the mailing list announces 2027.
duration: 8 weeks (June to July in 2026)
pay_detail: Described as a paid internship. The hourly amount is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 through 19. Co-ed. You do not need to be in top shape.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online interest card to get on the email list. You can send questions by email to the fire team at firerecruiting@austintexas.gov.
notes: Teams compete in the DFW Fire Games in the spring and the San Antonio fire games in the fall. Being an Explorer does not hurt you if you apply to be a firefighter later. There are also ways to volunteer.
duration: Weekend meetings, one day each weekend for several weeks before each competition
pay_detail: No pay or fee is stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 15 cannot go on active building sites. They do other projects, and there must be 1 adult for every 5 kids. Ages 16 and 17 may help build new homes. They may not use power tools or work above 6 feet. They must bring a parent or guardian over 21. Home Repair and Blitz Build need 18 or older.
how_to_apply: Look at the volunteer calendar (austinhabitat.volunteerhub.com) or the general sign-up page. The youth page does not give its own steps. Call Volunteer Services at 512-472-8788 ext. 106. Or write to volservices@austinhabitat.org.
notes: The age 12 start is for the project ideas listed for 12 and up. Confirm the right sign up path for your age with Volunteer Services.
duration: Family Build Days happen 3 to 4 times a year. Other timing is not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up. Ages 14 and 15 need a parent or guardian over 21 to train and volunteer with them at all times. Ages 16 and 17 can volunteer on their own with parental consent given on the online application.
how_to_apply: Pay the fee, go to a virtual welcome orientation, finish online training, then take a hands on training session and pick a shift. Start from the Get Started button on the volunteer page.
notes: The youth page does not list a fee, but the volunteer page does. This page does not cover the clinic volunteer program.
duration: At least 3 months, 2 hours per week
pay_detail: Unpaid. One time registration fee of $20 for students ($35 for adults), paid at orientation.

who_can_apply: Austin ISD students who will be in grades 10 to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Interest Form linked on the page. Students heard by March 30. They had to go to orientations in late April and mid May. Contact Cecilia Gutierrez at cecilia.gutierrez@austinisd.org.
notes: Info sessions in 2026 were held on Google Meet in December and January. The page lists the work period as ending July 23 in one place and July 24 in another.
duration: 6 weeks, about 20 hours a week (2026: June 8 to July 23, with a break June 29 to July 3)
pay_detail: $2,000 stipend for living expenses

who_can_apply: Teens age 15 to 17 living in Central Texas who will be a sophomore, junior or senior in the coming fall (homeschoolers welcome). Must be able to work legally in the U.S., or be willing to waive pay on a student-only visa. About 10 teens are hired each year.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Foundation's Teen Library Fellowship page when the application opens. Questions go to the Teen Librarian at kathleen.houlihan@austintexas.gov.
notes: Fellows must attend a mandatory monthly Sunday afternoon retreat at the Central Library; travel stipends are available. The Foundation page says ages 15-17 and $21 per hour; library pages say $22 per hour and one library page says ages 15-18, so confirm when applications open.
duration: 9 months (about August to May)
pay_detail: $21 per hour on the Foundation page ($22 per hour on the library pages), up to 10 hours of work per month

who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 17 (no younger than 13 and no older than 17 by Aug 1 for fall, Dec 1 for spring, or May 1 for summer). Must pass a background check (fingerprinting for ages 15+ who lived outside Texas in the last seven years) and attend a mandatory orientation.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application posted on the Teen Volunteer Program page during the window. There may be an interview with the volunteer coordinator; you get three business days to accept an offer. Not every applicant gets a placement.
notes: Placement depends on the library branch and supervisor, and the library gets more applicants than placements. Contact: APL.Volunteers@austintexas.gov. Limit of two absences per season.
duration: Fall (Oct-Dec) and spring (Mar-May): 10 weeks, one 2-hour shift a week. Summer (June-July): 8 weeks, one 2 to 4 hour shift a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students living in Central Texas, ages 16 to 18 (or turning 16 in the year they apply), interested in creative careers and Latinx issues, and able to work legally in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Submit a personal application, a portfolio and teacher recommendations, then do one-on-one and panel interviews. Questions: caminos@austintexas.gov.
notes: About 10 to 12 teens per cohort. Competitive. The page says the next round is expected in Spring 2027, with no exact date posted.
duration: 10 months, mid-to-late August through early June; most Saturdays 10:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. plus Wednesday evenings
pay_detail: $22.05 per hour, about 6 to 10 hours per week

who_can_apply: Lifeguard training and hiring starts at age 15 with no upper age limit. You need a physical Social Security card and Texas-issued ID for the in-person paperwork.
how_to_apply: Step 1: fill out the online lifeguard job application. Step 2: visit the Aquatic Office in person at 2818 San Gabriel St. with your Social Security card, Texas ID and any hiring paperwork emailed to you. Questions: 512-974-9330.
notes: The 2026 posting also offered a $200 stipend for guards trained and working 40 hours before July 4, 2026. One library list says age 16+; the Parks page (dated March 20, 2026) says 15. Texas hour limits apply to 15 year olds.
duration: Seasonal; training happens before the swim season
pay_detail: Starting at $22.05 per hour (March 2026 posting)

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18 (summer camp listing). The listing does not give other rules.
how_to_apply: Sign up through the city parks registration search for Roving Leaders, or call (512) 974-3927.
notes: Rides are available if you ask. The old city page for Roving Leaders no longer opens after the city site redesign, so this card uses the city sign-up listing. Not a job.
duration: Summer 2026 camp: June 8 to August 7, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 2 p.m.
pay_detail: Free. The summer camp listing shows a cost of $0.

who_can_apply: Teens. The Virginia L. Brown center listing says ages 13 to 18, and the Montopolis listing says grades 7 to 12. You must sign up first, and space is limited.
how_to_apply: Use the Register online link on the TCTA page, or call the rec center you want to go to. Centers include Dittmar, Dove Springs, Gus Garcia, Mendez, Montopolis, Northwest and Virginia L. Brown.
notes: Program contact: Clint Hofmeister, TCTA coordinator, 512-978-2476. Each center listing has its own staff contact. Not a job.
duration: After school. The Montopolis class meets Monday and Wednesday, 6 to 8 p.m. Other centers set their own times.
pay_detail: Free. The classes cost nothing.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 17. You register through the Austin and Travis County summer youth jobs program.
how_to_apply: Sign up ahead of time through the Travis County summer youth jobs program. SAFE links to it from its page. For questions, email Randy Randolph at Rrandolph@safeaustin.org or call 512-356-1633.
notes: SAFE also leads free talks in schools and clubs if you ask. The county jobs program may look at your family's income.
duration: 5 weeks, part-time
pay_detail: Paid part-time. The rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18. You must be 15 by June 1 and free for the whole program.
how_to_apply: Send the online volunteer application. If you are accepted, you get orientation and training details later. Email sdmc.volunteers@stdavids.com. Or call 512-544-4491.
notes: Records are required for 2 MMR doses, 2 chickenpox doses or history, Tdap within 10 years, a TB test within 90 days and a flu shot. Homeschooled teens may apply year round. Up to 2 service day absences may be requested ahead of time.
duration: 7 to 8 weeks, usually first week of June to end of July, two 4 hour shifts a week
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. You must be 16 by June 1 and available the whole program.
how_to_apply: Send the online application. Then you get an email asking for a teen and parent agreement, two letters of support, short essay answers and shot records. Teens who are picked get an invite to interview. Orientation is by invite. Email namc.volunteers@hcahealthcare.com or call 512-901-1223.
notes: St. David's Medical Center in central Austin has a separate teen program with different ages (15 to 18) and dates. Apply to the campus whose rules you meet.
duration: 7 to 8 weeks, usually first week of June to end of July. Weekly hours are not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Other rules are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: The VolunTeens link goes to an online volunteer form (Volgistics). The form needs JavaScript. Check it for the current steps.
notes: Thinkery also runs a teen Counselor in Training program for summer camps. Its page was not found (404), so it is not listed here. Check the dates, cost and application window before you apply. On 2026-10-10 the VolunTeens link went to a bare application form with no program text. So the 60 training hours, 40 service hours and 208 VolunTeen figures could not be checked again.
duration: 60 hours of training plus 40 hours of service
pay_detail: Volunteer service. Cost and pay are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: The page does not state ages, grades or school or home rules. It says applications are closed and to watch for future chances.
how_to_apply: No application is open now. Contact Urban Roots at info@urbanrootsatx.org or 512-750-8019 to ask when the next one opens.
notes: Details on this page are thin. The page does not name a Summer Farm Program. Ask about ages, pay and season before counting on it. The same page lists free elementary day camps (2nd to 5th grade) and a free middle school Food Lab, which are not for high schoolers.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Described as paid youth internships. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24 (out of school youth services target ages 16 to 24). The page says low income youth. For training scholarships and case managed help, the main page lists U.S. work authorization, living in Austin or Travis County, and one more need related to work, income or school.
how_to_apply: Click Get Started on the Youth Services page. It leads to the Jumpstart Your Career registration form and a career info session. You can also use the contact page or call your local career center.
notes: The Jumpstart form asks for the last four digits of a Social Security number. It uses them to check your info on WorkInTexas.com. Summer jobs through SEAL need year round part in WIOA. No income limit is listed.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Work experience is part of the services. Paid work experience is named only for the SEAL program (students with disabilities ages 16 to 22). Pay amounts are not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students who live in the City of Austin or its Extraterritorial Jurisdiction (ETJ). Students who only attend school in Austin are not eligible. No citizenship rule. A 2.5 GPA or higher is preferred, but applicants are read as a whole.
how_to_apply: Watch the page for the application in Spring 2027. Send questions to the program coordinator. Her email is abrianna.citta01@austintexas.gov.
notes: Members may attend national conferences each year, including one in Washington, D.C. The page does not say who pays for travel.
duration: Monthly meetings and service events. Term length is not stated on the page.
pay_detail: Pay is not mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 22 who live in the Austin and Travis County area. You need a reliable ride. You must be able to get a driver's license within 90 days. You must have a high school diploma or GED, or be working toward one.
how_to_apply: Complete the online interest form linked on the page. Call 512-972-4785 or email AYD@austintexas.gov.
notes: The page says the work is paid work with the City, plus mentoring and career planning. It does not give pay, hours, length or application dates. Call before applying. Office: 1416 Montopolis Drive, Austin.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Pay, hours and length are not listed on the page.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 16 to 20 who live in the City of Austin or its extraterritorial jurisdiction and are eligible to work legally in the U.S. No academic requirements.
how_to_apply: Online application (about 1.5 hours), short-answer questions, and one reference who completes a recommendation form. Accepted members become City of Austin employees and must verify work eligibility.
notes: Meetings are held at locations around Austin and transportation help may be available.
duration: One year, June to May; one full council meeting a month
pay_detail: $22.05 per hour, about 10 to 15 hours per month

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 16 years old who can volunteer at least six hours a month and is excited about Texas history and welcoming visitors.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. If it is approved you are contacted for an interview, then attend a New Volunteer Orientation.
notes: You must be 16 or older. If you are approved, they contact you for an interview. Then you go to a new volunteer orientation.
duration: At least 6 hours per month
pay_detail: Unpaid. After 25 hours of service volunteers can get a complimentary museum membership.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18, in good standing at school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the printable volunteer application on the program page. If accepted, pass a background check, drug screening and TB skin test, and attend orientation. Call (915) 263-5243.
notes: The page gives the March 15 to May 1 window as a yearly pattern, not as dates for 2027. Check the page in March.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 17 can join the Shelter Volunteer, Cats at the Zoo and Community Service programs. A parent or guardian must go to orientation and basic animal handling training. Teens 14 to 16 must volunteer with a parent or guardian. That adult must also be a registered volunteer.
how_to_apply: Send a volunteer form on the volunteer portal. Then finish orientation in person or in the MyImpact app. Email the volunteer team to book your first day.
notes: Teens 16 and 17 need a parent or guardian to take Level 1 Animal Handling Training too. Maybe you only need service hours for school or NHS. The page says you can email the volunteer team and skip onboarding.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18. Volunteers 13 to 17 need a parent or legal guardian to sign a waiver.
how_to_apply: Download the form from the program page and fill it out. Email it to EPHConnections@elpasohealth.com. The program page lists no phone number for the volunteer program.
notes: The program page lists last year's totals: 3,344 backpacks, 331,947 pounds of food and 404 car seats. The totals are not dated.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. Volunteers 17 and up must have a state-issued ID.
how_to_apply: Click the link on the program page. It goes to the City of El Paso volunteer page on governmentjobs.com. Apply there.
notes: The program page does not say which library branches need teen help. Call the Main Library at (915) 212-READ to ask.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24. Live in El Paso, Brewster, Culberson, Hudspeth, Jeff Davis or Presidio County. Be a U.S. citizen or allowed to work in the U.S. Males over 18 must be registered for Selective Service.
how_to_apply: Check the list of who can join on the program page. Then email nextforce@borderplexjobs.com. The bottom of the site also lists 915-887-2600.
notes: The program page says its help is most useful for veterans and military spouses. It is also useful for youth in foster care and young adults who left high school. The page lists a hiring event on Nov 10, 2026 from 10 AM to 2 PM at Bassett Place. The event is called Hiring Red, White & You.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. Work experience can be paid or unpaid. Gas money, uniforms and child care help are free.

who_can_apply: High school students 15 and older who can work on their own after training. Year round spots are few. They mostly go to homeschool, hybrid or similar students.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. You get an email in 24 to 48 hours with next steps. They are an interview with the Student Volunteer Committee, a background check, a drug test and shot records. Call 512-942-4777 or email sdghvolunteers@hcahealthcare.com.
notes: Georgetown is in Williamson County, north of Round Rock. Shifts can be evenings and weekends. Vaccines listed: flu, Tdap within 10 years, TB, 2 MMR and 2 chickenpox or history.
duration: 3 to 4 hours a week, up to 8 weeks in summer
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must be low income. You must meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules. You must meet background rules. You must be ready and motivated. The page does not explain rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Go to enroll.jobcorps.gov. Click Apply Now. Make a MyJobCorps account. Upload eligibility papers. Then have an interview with an admissions representative. Or call 800-733-5627.
notes: The center page footer lists 2800 Airport Hwy 21 E, San Marcos, TX 78667. Job Corps is a training program, not a job. Texas has other Job Corps centers that are not covered by this card.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Training is free. The national site lists free housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The allowance amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Tutors are ages 13 to 18, love working with young kids, have a B or higher in high school math, and bring a laptop.
how_to_apply: Sign up to volunteer on the OneInMath site. Use the register-volunteer page.
notes: The program pages do not list chapter locations. The tutor page's library news mentions North Texas libraries, so ask the group which library near you has a chapter. Re-check 2026-10-10: the tutor page does not say sign-up is ongoing, so status is unconfirmed, not rolling.
duration: 2 to 3 hours a week. Commit to at least one session, preferably a year.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Watch the library volunteer page for the application form. Questions go to Teen Librarian Jane Dance at jdance@roundrocktexas.gov or 512-218-7012.
notes: New members attend an orientation. Members also tidy and shelve on the 2nd floor.
duration: Meets monthly on the 4th Tuesday at 6:30 pm
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn community service hours and recognition.

who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 18 with strong customer service skills who check email daily and can commit to both June and July (no more than 7 days of vacation). Round Rock residents and Round Rock ISD students get priority. First time volunteers need a recommendation letter.
how_to_apply: Watch the library volunteer page for sign-up. Teen volunteers also need a parent signature and a volunteer agreement. They also go to an orientation. Contact Jane Dance at jdance@roundrocktexas.gov or 512-218-7012.
notes: General library teen volunteers must be at least 13. They must give at least 30 hours a year. They must bring a letter from a teacher, coach or a similar adult. If you worked a Summer Reading shift in the past two years, you are asked not to apply.
duration: June 1 to July 31 in 2026
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Must be 15 or older before the last class. Must pass a swim test: swim 150 yards, tread water 2 minutes, then swim 50 yards, and retrieve a 10 pound object from 7 to 10 feet.
how_to_apply: Sign up for training at roundrockrecreation.com. Then apply for jobs on the city job portal. To get the $75 rate, email the signed Commitment Letter to pardcustomerservice@roundrocktexas.gov. Call 512-218-5540 with questions.
notes: It is smart to apply early. If you pass the class, you get Lifeguard, CPR/AED and First Aid cards. They are good for 2 years. You must come to every class.
duration: Seasonal summer job. Training classes run November to May.
pay_detail: Lifeguard pay shown as $15 to $19.50 per hour (from a graphic on the page; a separate rate sheet is the official source). Training costs $215 to $305, or $75 if you sign a full season work commitment. Scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Youth in 3rd through 12th grade, ages 8 to 18. Each county sets up its own program.
how_to_apply: Contact your County Extension Office. Find a club. It needs at least five youth from three families. Choose at least one project. Then enroll online in 4HOnline.
notes: The October 31 date is the price cutoff, not a closing date. Counties customize their programs, so call your county Extension office first. This is a club and leadership program, not a paid job.
duration: One 4-H year. Every membership resets to inactive on August 15, so you re-enroll each year.
pay_detail: Youth fee is $25 if you enroll by October 31 and $30 from November 1 through the end of the 4-H year.

who_can_apply: Texas 4-H members in high school. STEM Ambassadors must be 15 or older. Photo Ambassadors must first finish training as a Junior Master Photographer.
how_to_apply: Pick a team on the Texas 4-H Ambassadors page, then use that team application or contact. Some teams post their details on their own sites.
notes: You need to be an enrolled 4-H member. The Water Ambassadors dates on the page looked out of date, so check that team's own site.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Older Texas 4-H members. Peers vote for district delegates. Six At-Large Delegates are voted in across the state.
how_to_apply: Send in the 2026-2027 At-Large Delegate application and the 2026-2027 Council Membership Contract. Or run in your district. Ask your District 4-H Specialist for the district due date.
notes: All delegates must sign the council contract for 2026-2027. Both kinds of delegate sign it.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Male high school students who finished their junior year. You need at least one semester left. You must never have been to Boys State. School officials must recommend you. You need a parent or guardian's permission. The sponsoring American Legion Post must certify you. You must sign the Texas Boys State Pledge.
how_to_apply: A school official nominates you. That can be a principal, teacher, coach or counselor. A local American Legion Post certifies and sponsors you. Ask your counselor or contact your local Post. The program's site is texasboysstate.com.
notes: Boys State is for boys. Girls State is a separate program. The site says the program asks for one or more boys nominated from each accredited public or private high school. Top delegates may be picked for Boys Nation. Confirm the 2027 dates and fee with your local Post.
duration: One week. The 2026 session ran Sunday June 7 to Friday June 12, 2026.
pay_detail: American Legion Posts or other community groups often pay the fee, so the cost to the boy is often little to nothing. The fee amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Female students now in their junior year at any Texas public or private high school. An ALA Unit may sponsor a home school student who meets the rules. You can attend only once. A student whose religion does not allow her to pledge allegiance to the U.S. flag is not eligible. You must be able to take part in all activities.
how_to_apply: You do not apply on your own. A school nominates you through faculty and a school official, and a local ALA Unit, the school or a community group reserves the spot. Ask your counselor or a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit early in the spring. Questions: GirlsState@alatexas.org or 214-733-7945.
notes: Girls State is for girls. Texas Boys State is a separate program run by the American Legion. Students chosen must attend the whole session to earn the certificate and pin.
duration: One week. The 2026 session was Sunday June 14 to Saturday June 20, 2026.
pay_detail: The 2026 fee was $550 per delegate, not including travel to Seguin. Rules say a unit, school or community group pays it, never the student or her family.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17, from incoming 8th graders to incoming seniors. Apply as a Cadet. Past camp graduates can later apply as Assistant Leaders.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application with two essay questions and a list of achievements. Rank your top three camp choices.
notes: Camp phone 210-556-1391. Assistant Leaders can earn college scholarships. Camps listed for 2026 include Bobwhite, Buckskin, Ranch, Bass, Waterfowl and Coastal Brigades.
duration: 5 days
pay_detail: Camp price not stated on the program pages. The site says tuition help is available. Email camps@texasbrigades.org.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 15 and a half to 18 who are U.S. citizens and Texas residents and are physically and mentally able to take part fully. The program is for youth who are currently disengaged from school.
how_to_apply: Go to an information briefing with a recruiter. Send the application packet and documents. Do a virtual interview with a case manager. Have a mentor fill out a mentor packet. Then a review board decides. Main line: 877-822-0050.
notes: This is for teens who are off track in school, not a job program. Campus: 600 HWY 3013 West, Eagle Lake, TX 77434.
duration: The page lists a tuition-free 22-week residential program. It also lists a 20-week Residential Phase and a 5 and a half month on-campus phase, then a 12-month Post-Residential Phase. The page says the program requires a 17 and a half month commitment. Confirm with a recruiter.
pay_detail: Free. The page says the program is tuition free to the families it serves.

who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 15 by June 1 of the program year and enrolled in high school for the next school year. The flyer describes the program as ages 15 to 17.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, upload two recommendation letters from two different references, and upload your most recent report card. Accepted volunteers must show vaccine records (MMR, varicella, Tdap) and a negative TB test, and attend mandatory orientation on the first two days.
notes: The flyer calls the program prestigious and highly sought-after, so expect competition. Up to two absences are allowed. There are no weekend or make-up shifts. Questions: ATXNCVolunteerServices@texaschildrens.org or 737-229-3388. Check the Texas Children's volunteer pages for the 2027 flyer.
duration: About 4 weeks, Monday to Thursday 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (June 1 to June 25 in 2026)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program

who_can_apply: Students at a Texas high school with a DECA chapter. Texas DECA members must take part in a career and technical education (CTE) program. Chapters must offer business or marketing courses. The official pages list no age or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's DECA advisor, who registers members through DECA's online system. If your school has no chapter, DECA lists six steps to start one. State advisor: Josh Shankle, shankle@texasdeca.org. State office phone: 817-900-8037.
notes: DECA's page lists 352 Texas high school chapters. The state website does not explain joining step by step, so start with your school's advisor.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Student membership is $16 total: $8 to the state association and $8 to DECA Inc. Chapters may add local costs.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12, or the home school match. You join a team of five from the same school or group. The team has an adult advisor.
how_to_apply: Contact the Texas Envirothon office at 281-283-3045 or reistle@uhcl.edu. Then send in the sign-up packet and the fee. You must show proof of health insurance.
notes: Teams need an adult advisor plus chaperones of each gender. The school or group pays for travel, meals and lodging. Teams with fewer than five can play but may lose points on the oral part.
duration: 3 day state event
pay_detail: A non-refundable team registration fee is required each year. The amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Students who sign up for an agricultural science class at a school with an FFA chapter. The FAQ says the grade depends on the district and that home-schooled students are not covered by the program. Junior FFA needs age 8 and 3rd grade.
how_to_apply: Your first contact is your local agricultural science teacher. Sign up for an agricultural science class.
notes: Junior FFA is a state-only membership at $9 a year, says the membership page.
duration: School year, tied to your agricultural science class
pay_detail: National dues $7 plus Texas dues $9 is $16 a year, not counting area, district or local dues. Junior FFA is $9 a year (state only).

who_can_apply: Secondary students in a state-approved Health Science program, or who plan a career in the health professions. Middle school students in grades 6 to 8 who like a health career path can also join. Membership goes through affiliated school chapters.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's health science teacher or chapter advisor about joining the chapter. State office: texashosa@texashosa.org or 1-877-728-0150.
notes: State office: 201 W. Hillside Road Suite 26, Laredo, TX 78041. Ask your advisor for the fee amount and conference dates.
duration: School year
pay_detail: There are membership fees, but the amounts are not on the program pages. The site links to a 2026 to 2027 fee schedule.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. Anyone under 16 must come with a parent or guardian. Everyone under 18 needs a parent or guardian's signed permission, and a parent signs the liability waiver. Each opening can add its own requirements. Minors cannot do some kinds of work.
how_to_apply: Search openings in the TPWD volunteer portal and apply online. Or contact a park's volunteer coordinator. TPWD checks your application and matches you to an opening. Questions: Volunteer@TPWD.Texas.gov or 512-389-8674.
notes: Park host jobs are long RV-based stays and are not a fit for most teens. The page lists Buffalo Soldiers, State Park Ambassadors and Texas Outdoor Family as special programs, but this card does not cover their age rules. Volunteers 18 and older in ongoing roles must pass a yearly background check.
duration: Varies by opening
pay_detail: Unpaid. The FAQ mentions no volunteer fees or costs.

who_can_apply: High school students who finished at least one high school chemistry course before the summer. The pages give no grade, age or residency rule. You need a recommendation from a high school chemistry teacher. Selection is merit based and space is limited to 20 students.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, which includes a short chemistry research statement. The form sends a request to your chemistry teacher for the recommendation. Questions: tamu_react@tamu.edu.
notes: The program ran for the first time in 2025 (July 14 to 25). The fee and rules above come from the 2026 pages, so check them again when the 2027 application opens. The program site is a Google Sites page run by the department.
duration: The 2026 header lists July 13 to 24, 2026 and also calls it a 6-day in-person program. The 2027 dates are not posted.
pay_detail: Applying is free. The registration fee is $250, due after you are accepted (2026 page). Lunch is provided.

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 22 (and under 22 as of September 1 of the previous year) who get special education services under IDEA or have a disability under Section 504, and who are in an educational program. That includes secondary school, home school and other recognized programs.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Texas Workforce Solutions Vocational Rehabilitation Services office. Counselors refer current VR participants. Students who have not applied for VR but meet the disability rule may also be candidates. Statewide contact: 512-936-6400 or vr.office.locator@twc.texas.gov.
notes: Only for students with disabilities. Texas child labor hour limits for 14 and 15 year olds still apply. The pages do not give a posted 2027 timeline.
duration: At least five weeks of paid work, with at least four hours in a week to count as a week. No more than 40 hours a week.
pay_detail: Wages for hours worked. Each local board sets one hourly wage for its program. The amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 through 18. You must be in school or a graduate with a satisfactory record. You must be unmarried (except marriage under 18) and not on active duty. You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (headquarters may waive). You must be of good moral character. Cadets who join before age 19 can stay until 21.
how_to_apply: Pick a local squadron from the Texas Wing unit listing. Go to three squadron meetings as a trial. The squadron and higher headquarters must accept you. Call Wing headquarters at 936-205-9013 with questions.
notes: Meeting times differ by squadron. This is a youth program, not a paid job.
duration: Year-round program with squadron meetings, plus encampments and other events
pay_detail: National Civil Air Patrol page: annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location, and about $300 to $600 in costs in the first year, less any financial assistance. Ask your squadron for exact costs.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 18 from across Texas.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked from the workshop website. Questions: tssrmyrw@gmail.com.
notes: Check the site for the 2027 application. Sponsor contacts: Dorian Damerau 830-387-8429 or Jr. Tompkins 979-541-3411.
duration: 1 week
pay_detail: Program fee not stated on the page. Organizers say they can help applicants find sponsors.

who_can_apply: Must be 14 to 18 (14 by April 1) and in middle or high school, and must live and/or attend school in Travis County. Teens with disabilities can apply up to age 22. Other factors such as household income may also be considered.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application (Jotform) and upload a Social Security card and a school ID or recent report card. Eligible applicants are invited to a mandatory job readiness training, then matched to a host site if space allows. Applying does not guarantee a placement.
notes: Phone 512-854-4590, syep@traviscountytx.gov. Up to 750 paid spots each year. Pay rate and hours are not stated on the page. The page does not mention a work permit. Texas rules for 14 and 15 year olds limit hours (see Texas Workforce Commission child labor page). The SAFE Alliance Summer Youth Leadership Academy also hires through this program.
duration: 5 to 7 weeks
pay_detail: Paid work experience; hourly rate not stated on the program page

who_can_apply: Current or rising high school students who are interested in a medical career and can attend in person from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. every day.
how_to_apply: The program page does not describe an application. It says students hear about the camp when staff visit high schools in the El Paso region. Call René André at 915-215-4408.
notes: The program page has a link named Summer Med Camp Mentor. The page gives no details about that role.
duration: Two weeks per session
pay_detail: Snacks and learning materials are free. Camp cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Texas residents are prioritized. You must be 15 or older by June 1, 2027 and available all five weeks. In person only. You arrange your own housing and transportation.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the application opens in mid January 2027. First round notices go out at the end of April and second round in early May, with a deposit due one week after you accept. Email hsra@utexas.edu.
notes: This costs a lot and is hard to get into. The page says a few need-based scholarships may be available. They give a stipend plus free tuition. There are no merit scholarships now. Your lab spot is based on your interests, your free time and space. Full tuition is due in mid May.
duration: 5 weeks, June 7 to July 14, 2027 (off June 18 and July 5)
pay_detail: Summer 2027 tuition is $4,500. Payment is due only after you accept a lab placement. Financial aid is not mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. Participation does not guarantee admission to UT Austin.
how_to_apply: Click the Apply Now button on the UT page. Summer Discovery, not UT, handles applications and sign-up. You can email summerdiscovery@utexas.edu. Or call 516-447-4907.
notes: Expensive. Students get a certificate of completion and a campus grade letter. The Summer Discovery page shows an early enrollment discount ending Oct 31 but does not say the year.
duration: 2 week or 3 week sessions (2026: June 14 to 26 and June 28 to July 17)
pay_detail: Costs $3,799 to $7,999 depending on the options chosen (the Summer Discovery page gives one range). Some courses add fees. Financial aid is not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Students entering 8th or 9th grade. A panel reviews applications (not first come, first served), and students who attend schools without engineering or STEM offerings are encouraged to apply. Houston and San Antonio sessions are by invitation only.
how_to_apply: Register through the camp page; you are notified by email by mid-May. Questions: cseoutreach@utexas.edu.
notes: For younger teens (about 13 to 15). Both 2026 Austin sessions are listed as full.
duration: 4 days (Austin sessions June 8-11 and July 6-9 in 2026; both were full)
pay_detail: $75 commitment fee for Austin participants, collected only after acceptance (day camp, no lodging)

who_can_apply: Current Texas high school sophomores and juniors. Students who are in summer school on the program dates cannot take part. Chosen students usually have a strong school record and personal wins.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for a transcript, your activities and leadership, essays, a letter of support and a resume. The Apply link on the page was a placeholder. Email SummerPrograms@mccombs.utexas.edu or call 512-475-7340.
notes: Texas high school students only. Shared McCombs page for three programs. Decisions are released by mid April.
duration: June 20 to 25, 2027 on the UT Austin campus, with on campus living
pay_detail: Free. The page says educational, food and boarding costs are covered. Students pay their own travel to and from campus.

who_can_apply: Current Texas high school sophomores and juniors. Students who are in summer school on the program dates cannot take part. Chosen students usually have a strong school record and personal wins.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for a transcript, your activities and leadership, essays, a letter of support and a resume. The Apply link on the page was a placeholder. Email SummerPrograms@mccombs.utexas.edu or call 512-475-7340.
notes: Texas high school students only. Shared McCombs page for three programs. Decisions are released by mid April.
duration: June 6 to 11, 2027 on the UT Austin campus, with on campus living
pay_detail: Free. The page says educational, food and boarding costs are covered. Students pay their own travel to and from campus.

who_can_apply: Texas high school juniors only. Students who are in summer school on the program dates cannot take part. Chosen students usually have a strong school record and personal wins.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for a transcript, your activities and leadership, essays, a letter of support and a resume. The Apply link on the page was a placeholder. Email SummerPrograms@mccombs.utexas.edu or call 512-475-7340.
notes: Texas high school students only. Shared McCombs page for three programs. Decisions are released by mid April. More info: https://www.mccombs.utexas.edu/undergraduate/subiendo/
duration: June 13 to 17, 2027 on the UT Austin campus, with on campus living
pay_detail: Free. The page says educational, food and boarding costs are covered. Travel is covered by the program.

who_can_apply: High school students going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade. You should like STEM jobs and mining engineering.
how_to_apply: The program page has a Get Notified for Future Camps option. Email miningengineering@utep.edu. Or call 915-747-7057.
notes: No 2027 dates are posted on the program page.
duration: 3 days per session
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school students at schools in the program. Low-income students who could be the first in their family to go to college must qualify. Schools: Bel Air, Del Valle, Parkland, Riverside and Ysleta (YISD). Also Eastlake, El Dorado, Fabens, Pebble Hills, Socorro and Tornillo (SFT ISDs).
how_to_apply: Not stated on the program page. Email upwardbound@utep.edu or call (915) 747-5062.
notes: Federally funded. Students must qualify to be selected. This is a college prep program, not a job.
duration: Through high school graduation and the first summer semester at UTEP
pay_detail: Free to students.

who_can_apply: Students ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: Email the Volunteer Coordinator at elpcdce@va.gov. Ask about the summer youth program.
notes: The program page says applications open in May but gives no 2027 dates.
duration: June through August
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
